data.rationale: Fuzz target exrcorecheck_fuzzer calls checkOpenEXRFile(data,size,true,true,true), driving runCoreChecks -> checkCoreFile -> readCoreScanlinePart. Here the output buffer imgdata is sized once (line 1252-1260) as sum over channels of width * user_bytes_per_element * lines_per_chunk, where lines_per_chunk comes from exr_get_scanlines_per_chunk (a fixed value from the compression type). However the decoder pipeline is initialized/updated from per-chunk info (exr_read_scanline_chunk_info) and exr_decoding_run writes using cinfo-derived chunk geometry. If a crafted header declares a chunk covering more scanlines/bytes than lines_per_chunk*width*bpp (e.g. mismatched chunk/packed size or compression), the decode writes past the end of imgdata, a classic heap-buffer-overflow. The TODO comment at line 1256 ('check we are supposed to multiply by lines per chunk above') further signals this sizing is the suspect code. Same sizing pattern repeats in readCoreTiledPart (lines 1392-1412).
